0.text: The process starts on the customer side with the selection of the desired chainsaw properties, which is sent to the manufacturer. The manufacturer starts by receiving and analyzing the order, then orders the required parts from suppliers and awaits their delivery; if not all parts are received, the manufacturer checks with suppliers and continues receiving deliveries until everything has arrived. Once all parts are in, the order is manually inspected and the chainsaw is assembled. The manufacturer then sends the first product to the customer and provides regular updates, while waiting for the customer’s feedback. Based on the feedback, either the product is improved and another first product is sent for review, or the manufacturer proceeds by splitting work into producing the rest of the order and monitoring progress in parallel, continuing to send regular updates. When both production and monitoring have finished, the complete order is sent to the customer. The customer receives the order and their process ends, and the manufacturer’s process ends afterward. Communications with suppliers occur when parts are ordered and when the manufacturer checks with them, and suppliers deliver the parts to the manufacturer.

0.text: Three parties interact. At the company, the process starts with receiving a job application. The company then proceeds with two actions in parallel: it confirms the application and rates the application; once both are completed, it decides whether to proceed. If the decision is declined, the company ends without an employee. If accepted, the company negotiates an interview, then assesses the job seeker and decides again: if declined, it ends without an employee; if accepted, it hires the candidate and ends with an employee found. In parallel, the job platform starts by sending job offers to the job seeker and, after analyzing status reports it receives from the seeker, forwards applications. When it forwards an application, it also awaits, in parallel, the company’s application rating and job confirmation; once both are received, it decides whether to proceed. If this decision is declined, it sends new job offers again. If accepted, it collects, in parallel, the seeker’s rating of the company and the company’s rating of the seeker; after both are in, it decides whether the job is successfully conveyed. If the combined outcome is that the company is rated better than C and the seeker has accepted, it ends with a conveyed job; otherwise, it sends new job offers again. On the job seeker side, the process starts by reporting application status to the platform, then reviewing job offers received from the platform, and applying. After applying, the seeker decides whether to accept; if declined, they report their status again and re-enter the offer review. If accepted, they enter a probation phase and rate the company; depending on that rating, if the company is rated C or less, they return to reviewing offers, while if it is better than C they move to a permanent job and end with a job found. The communications between parties are: the platform sends offers to the seeker; the seeker sends status reports to the platform; the seeker sends an application to the platform, which forwards it to the company; the company sends the job confirmation and the application rating to the platform; later, the company sends its rating of the seeker to the platform, and the seeker sends their rating of the company to the platform.

The test pilot then provides a test flight protocol, which is received and automatically forwarded to the customer. Next, shipping is arranged based on the customer type: premium customers receive premium shipping, otherwise standard shipping is used; after shipping, an email confirmation from the customer is awaited. 0.text: The process starts when the user opens Battle.net. The user then determines whether an account is already registered: if not, the user enters account information. Battle.net sends a confirmation email, and the user clicks the link in that message, after which the user proceeds to log into Battle.net. If the account was already registered, the user goes straight to logging in. After login, account information is loaded and the status of the World of Warcraft subscription is checked. If the subscription is active, the user proceeds directly toward logging into the game. If it is not active, the user selects a payment option and chooses a payment method: either entering credit card information or entering IBAN and BIC. After completing the chosen payment details, the flow continues to the same point as with an active subscription. The user then logs into the game, ingame data and the player’s position are loaded, and three choices are completed in parallel: the realm is selected, the race is selected, and the class is selected. Once all three have been chosen, the character is named. Battle.net then sends a confirmation and selfies to the user, and the process ends.
